markets.rules_primary: If the value of the S&P 500 index, as calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, on December 22, 2026 at 10:14:59 AM EST is at least 6800.00, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Observation: Uses the closing index level of the one-minute candle ending Dec 22, 2026 at 10:15am EST: the S&P 500 value as of 10:14:59 AM EST on December 22, 2026, the preceding minute's final second. Each market compares that same observation with its stated fixed index-point strike. At least includes equality, which resolves Yes. The named economic event provides context; a delayed or rescheduled release does not automatically move the observation time.

Source Agencies (in priority order): S&P Dow Jones Indices, Pyth Network (official S&P 500 feeds), Bloomberg, WSJ, TradingView, Yahoo Finance, CNBC. If sources conflict, this order governs; any remaining dispute is resolved by Kalshi under Rule 7.1.

What counts as the S&P 500 value:
Only the index level calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, to two decimal places.
ETFs, futures, options, perpetuals, and constituent stock prices do not count.
If no time of day is specified, the official closing value for each trading day is used. Intraday, open, high/low, and pre-/after-hours values do not count.

Trading days:
Only days with an official S&P 500 close count (Eastern Time). Weekends and market holidays are ignored.
If the specified observation is at or after an early close or a halt ending trading for the day, the official close designated by S&P Dow Jones Indices governs.

Index changes:
Changes to constituents, weightings, divisor, or methodology do not affect the contract.
If the index is renamed, rebranded, or re-coded but its record continues, the contract stays open. If it is discontinued with no successor, the No-data rule applies.

No data:
If no Source Agency publishes a value by the Expiration Date (including if markets are closed for the entire period), all markets resolve No, unless a "No data" strike is listed, in which case that strike resolves Yes.

Corrections:
Corrections published before Expiration govern; corrections published after Expiration are ignored.
If Kalshi finds a material error, it may delay Expiration until a corrected value is published. If none is published by the Expiration Date, the No-data rule applies.

Observation precision: If the exact-second index level is unavailable, the same-minute precision permitted by the contract applies. A different-time or stale price is not an automatic substitute.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the S&P Dow Jones Indices. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

Observation: Uses the closing index level of the one-minute candle ending Dec 22, 2026 at 10:15am EST: the S&P 500 value as of 10:14:59 AM EST on December 22, 2026, the preceding minute's final second. Each market compares that same observation with its stated fixed index-point strike. At least includes equality, which resolves Yes. The named economic event provides context; a delayed or rescheduled release does not automatically move the observation time.

What counts as the S&P 500 value:
Only the index level calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, to two decimal places.
ETFs, futures, options, perpetuals, and constituent stock prices do not count.
If no time of day is specified, the official closing value for each trading day is used. Intraday, open, high/low, and pre-/after-hours values do not count.

Trading days:
Only days with an official S&P 500 close count (Eastern Time). Weekends and market holidays are ignored.
If the specified observation is at or after an early close or a halt ending trading for the day, the official close designated by S&P Dow Jones Indices governs.

Index changes:
Changes to constituents, weightings, divisor, or methodology do not affect the contract.
If the index is renamed, rebranded, or re-coded but its record continues, the contract stays open. If it is discontinued with no successor, the No-data rule applies.

No data:
If no Source Agency publishes a value by the Expiration Date (including if markets are closed for the entire period), all markets resolve No, unless a "No data" strike is listed, in which case that strike resolves Yes.

Corrections:
Corrections published before Expiration govern; corrections published after Expiration are ignored.
If Kalshi finds a material error, it may delay Expiration until a corrected value is published. If none is published by the Expiration Date, the No-data rule applies.

Observation precision: If the exact-second index level is unavailable, the same-minute precision permitted by the contract applies. A different-time or stale price is not an automatic substitute.

markets.rules_primary: If the value of the S&P 500 index, as calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, on December 18, 2026 at 10:14:59 AM EST is at least 6800.00, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Observation: Uses the closing index level of the one-minute candle ending Dec 18, 2026 at 10:15am EST: the S&P 500 value as of 10:14:59 AM EST on December 18, 2026, the preceding minute's final second. Each market compares that same observation with its stated fixed index-point strike. At least includes equality, which resolves Yes. The named economic event provides context; a delayed or rescheduled release does not automatically move the observation time.

Source Agencies (in priority order): S&P Dow Jones Indices, Pyth Network (official S&P 500 feeds), Bloomberg, WSJ, TradingView, Yahoo Finance, CNBC. If sources conflict, this order governs; any remaining dispute is resolved by Kalshi under Rule 7.1.

What counts as the S&P 500 value:
Only the index level calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, to two decimal places.
ETFs, futures, options, perpetuals, and constituent stock prices do not count.
If no time of day is specified, the official closing value for each trading day is used. Intraday, open, high/low, and pre-/after-hours values do not count.

Trading days:
Only days with an official S&P 500 close count (Eastern Time). Weekends and market holidays are ignored.
If the specified observation is at or after an early close or a halt ending trading for the day, the official close designated by S&P Dow Jones Indices governs.

Index changes:
Changes to constituents, weightings, divisor, or methodology do not affect the contract.
If the index is renamed, rebranded, or re-coded but its record continues, the contract stays open. If it is discontinued with no successor, the No-data rule applies.

No data:
If no Source Agency publishes a value by the Expiration Date (including if markets are closed for the entire period), all markets resolve No, unless a "No data" strike is listed, in which case that strike resolves Yes.

Corrections:
Corrections published before Expiration govern; corrections published after Expiration are ignored.
If Kalshi finds a material error, it may delay Expiration until a corrected value is published. If none is published by the Expiration Date, the No-data rule applies.

Observation precision: If the exact-second index level is unavailable, the same-minute precision permitted by the contract applies. A different-time or stale price is not an automatic substitute.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the S&P Dow Jones Indices. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

markets.rules_secondary: This market covers only CPI releases scheduled to occur in calendar year 2026 and does not include the CPI release scheduled for January 2027, even though that release may report December 2026 data. The last covered CPI release is the November 2026 CPI release, scheduled for Thursday, December 10, 2026 at 8:30 AM ET.

“Core goods CPI” means “Commodities less food and energy commodities” in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), U.S. city average, as published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

Resolution uses the seasonally adjusted month-over-month percent change for November 2026 published in the first BLS CPI release reporting that month’s data, at its published precision. The value will not be recalculated from index levels. Subsequent revisions, including revisions to seasonal adjustments, will not affect resolution.
markets.title: Will seasonally adjusted month-over-month percentage change in core goods CPI for November 2026 be above 0.3%?
